name: Punan Bah-Biau
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: A Comprehensive Classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa (Punan Bah data pp. 111-124 per Glottolog)
earlier_scan.note: Smith 2017 contains Punan Bah material and may state stress

sources.citation: Melai, Zeckqualine & Norazuna Norahim. 2025. Pengenalan kepada Sistem Vokal Bahasa Punan. PENDETA Journal of Malay Language, Education and Literature 16(1): 201-214. doi:10.37134/pendeta.vol16.1.17.2025
sources.note: First-hand Punan Bah (Belaga) vowel study with Praat: 7 vowels, 4 diphthongs, 2 triphthongs, nasalisation, labialisation, vowel lengthening. Only prosodic remark (p. 210): non-contrastive lengthening of /i u/ in word-final syllables closed by /ŋ/, attributed to 'penekanan bunyi' (emphasis); 'tekanan' appears once in a generic definition citing Asmah 2019. No statement of where word stress falls.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2022 [2023]. Reconstructing non-contrastive stress in Austronesian and the role of the mora in stress shift, gemination and vowel shift. Diachronica 40(1): 111-152.
sources.note: No Punan language in the sample (grep 'Punan' = 0 hits); nearby Sekapan treated, not Punan Bah.

sources.citation: Melai, Zeckqualine & Ivy Anak Rigar. 2021. Phonological Documentation of the Punan Language: A Preliminary Study. JALA, The Journal of Asian Linguistic Anthropology 3(3): 1-18. doi:10.47298/jala.v3-i3-a1
sources.note: First-hand Punan Ba' data: 18 consonants, 6 vowels, 4 diphthongs, 2 triphthongs, vowel distribution, non-phonemic long [a:] in monosyllables (taan, maan, nyaan, daan). The words stress/accent/penult do not occur; silent on word stress.

sources.citation: Melai, Zeckqualine & Alvy Rigar. 2019. Moribund Language Documentation and Preservation: A Preliminary Study on the Punan Language. GLOCAL CALA 2019 Proceedings, 239-244. doi:10.47298/cala2019.6-6
sources.note: Sociolinguistic/ethnonym background (8 Punan longhouses, speech registers); no phonology; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: A comprehensive classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. xxii+701 pp. (sec. 2.4 'The Punan subgroup', printed pp. 111-127, incl. 2.4.4 'More on Punan Bah', Table 36 Punan Bah vowels, 2.4.4.2 triphthongs)
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Nothing for Punan Bah: primary Punan Bah field data are used for historical phonology (off-glides before velars, *a raising, triphthongs ey/ow, six-vowel table) but 'stress' never occurs in the Punan sections; stress is discussed only for Merap, Segai-Modang, Murik, Hliboi Bidayuh and W. Kalimantan Malayic. Fn. 10 p. 111 uses 'accent' only in the lay sense (Kalimantan Punan listeners found the Punan Bah recording had an unfamiliar accent).

sources.citation: Blust, Robert & Alexander D. Smith. 2014. A bibliography of the languages of Borneo (and Madagascar). Phillips, ME: Borneo Research Council.
sources.note: Bibliography: Punan Ba' entries are Clayre 1972a (Sarawak Gazette note), Needham 1955a (JMBRAS), Wilson 1972 comparative vocabulary; no grammar or phonology of Punan Bah exists in the list.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 2013. The Austronesian Languages (revised ed.). Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics.
sources.note: Punan Bah not mentioned (only Punan Batu in a language list).

sources.citation: Rensch, Calvin R. 2012. Melanau and the Languages of Central Sarawak. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2012-011. Dallas: SIL International. 100 pp.
sources.note: Comparative-lexical study; Punan Ba forms only from published wordlists (Urquhart 1955, Kaboy 1965, Ray 1913); nothing on stress.
